Seminar Title:

Power- and QoS-aware Resource Orchestration Framework for Cell-Free massive MIMO in 5G O-RAN

Abstract:

For power- and quality of service (QOS)-aware operation of cell-free massive multiple input multiple output (CF-mMIMO) in practical fifth-generation (5G) networks, end-to-end resource orchestration across the radio site, optical fronthaul, and virtualized cloud is required. In line with the cloudification and disaggregation principles of open radio access network (O-RAN), this work proposes a joint energy- and latency-aware resource orchestration framework for CF-mMIMO deployed over an O-RAN architecture with Time- and Wavelength-Division Multiplexed Passive Optical Network (TWDM-PON) fronthaul. A comprehensive end-to-end latency model is developed by considering over-the-air transmission delay, TWDM-PON fronthaul queuing and propagation delay, and O-Cloud General Purpose Processor (GPP) processing delay for both functional split Option 8 and Option 7.2. 5G network is divided into three slices, such as ultra low latency communication (uRLLC), enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB), and massive machine type communication (mMTC), and their latency budgets for 5G networks are 1 ms, 4 ms, and 10 ms, respectively. In the proposed end-to-end resource orchestration technique, the objective is to minimize network power consumption by considering virtualized cloud processing resources, optical fronthaul, and radio, while satisfying signal-to-noise-plus-interference ratio (SINR) and slice-specific latency constraints for each user equipment (UE). We propose an optimization model and a concave-convex procedure (CCP)- based heuristic to minimize the total power consumption of the networks by maximizing the total spectral efficiency while satisfying the required QoS of UEs. The proposed scheme is also compared with two baseline approaches: &rdquoradio-only&rdquo orchestration, in which radio resources are optimized independently of the cloud and fronthaul, and &rdquolocal coordination&rdquo orchestration, in which orchestration is restricted to a local cluster of open-radio units (O-RUs). The numerical results show that our proposed end-to-end orchestration method with fully virtualized fronthaul and cloud resources achieves substantial power savings compared to radio-only orchestration and local coordination, by up to 28% and 15%, respectively.
